standard.title: Character form and function, sentence structures and syntax
standard.description: apply knowledge of character form and function, sentence structures, syntax, and writing system features to infer meaning and to compose a range of texts
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can use morphological knowledge to infer meaning in unfamiliar words and apply complex grammatical structures in extended texts (AC9LCH6U02). They have composed texts across familiar and some unfamiliar contexts. They have not yet applied grammatical knowledge to modal, tense-expression, exclamatory and response-to-negative-question structures, used digital input methods for the writing system, or composed a full range of sentence types — affirmative, negative, interrogative, imperative — systematically.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students apply knowledge of character form and function, sentence structures, syntax and writing system features to infer meaning and compose a range of texts — including modal structures, tense-expression patterns, and varied sentence types.

nodes.label: Advanced morphological application and digital input
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can apply morphological knowledge to create new words and use digital input methods for the target language writing system.
nodes.minimum_width: Create at least three new compound words using known morphemes (verified as accurate), and demonstrate use of at least one digital input method for the target language writing system.
nodes.typical_width: Use morphological knowledge to create new words and confirm combinations using dictionaries or digital tools; use digital input methods for the writing system; categorise words by shared morpheme; use dictionary resources to understand subtle differences in word use.
wider: Investigate a productive morpheme in the target language — identify all the words it appears in, document the semantic pattern, and generate new combinations with verification
Compare digital input methods for the target language writing system — evaluate which method best suits different writing contexts (speed, accuracy, character discovery)
nodes.hinge_reason: Advanced morphological application and digital input are the productive writing prerequisites for Y7-8 text composition. Students who cannot generate words morphologically or use digital input methods are significantly constrained in both written output quantity and quality.

response_modes.reason: Digital input and morphological word creation require repeated practice for accuracy and speed. Regular writing tasks that require students to use both skills — not occasional demonstrations — build the productive fluency the descriptor requires.

success_criteria: Creates at least three new compound words using known morphemes, verified as accurate
Demonstrates competent use of at least one digital input method for the target language

nodes.label: Modal, tense-expression and exclamatory structures
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can recognise and use modal verbs, tense-expression patterns, and exclamatory structures in the target language, understanding how these differ from English equivalents.
nodes.minimum_width: Produce at least four sentences demonstrating different modal or tense-expression structures correctly, including at least one exclamatory or response-to-negative-question construction.
nodes.typical_width: Use modal verbs to express ability, permission and obligation; use tense-expression patterns — completion, experience, intention, negation — appropriately; construct exclamatory sentences and understand their purpose; understand response conventions for negative tag questions; compare these structures with English equivalents.
wider: Analyse how tense and aspect are expressed differently in the target language compared with English verb conjugation — create examples demonstrating each pattern and explain the difference
Investigate how response conventions for negative questions can cause miscommunication between target language and English speakers — create examples and explain the cultural and linguistic logic

response_modes.reason: Modal and tense-expression structures require explicit instruction because they differ systematically from English — students cannot rely on L1 transfer. Explicit comparison with English equivalents, followed by targeted production practice, prevents persistent structural errors.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Background learners often use these structures correctly in speech but cannot analyse or explain them. Width investment here builds the metalinguistic understanding that allows students to use these structures consciously in writing — bridging the gap between oral fluency and written accuracy.
success_criteria: Produces at least four sentences demonstrating different modal or tense-expression structures correctly
Constructs at least one exclamatory sentence and explains its purpose

nodes.label: Full sentence-type range in composed texts
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can compose texts using the full range of sentence types — affirmative, negative, interrogative, imperative — and apply full writing system and syntactic knowledge across a range of text types.
nodes.minimum_width: Compose a text using at least three different sentence types correctly, with appropriate punctuation and writing system conventions throughout.
nodes.typical_width: Construct and use affirmative, negative, interrogative and imperative sentences for different purposes; apply understanding of word order and sentence construction including target language-specific grammatical structures; compose texts across a range of types applying full grammatical knowledge.
wider: Analyse a model text and annotate every sentence for type, modal/tense structure, and syntactic feature — then compose an equivalent text using the same full syntactic repertoire
Create a text that deliberately uses each sentence type for a different communicative function — explain how each type serves a purpose in the overall text

response_modes.reason: Full sentence-type range in composed texts integrates morphological production (node 1) and modal/tense structure knowledge (node 2) into complete compositional competence. The teaching investment is in extended writing tasks that require varied sentence types — not only narrative or only information tasks, but the full communicative range.

success_criteria: Composes a text using at least three different sentence types with correct syntax
Applies appropriate punctuation and writing system conventions throughout the text
